podcast.body: Recorded with the band The Country of Miracles, this song begins with a meteorological observation from a farmer, stating that "an East Wind is the laziest wind. It doesn't go around you. It goes through you," which Downie noted was almost verbatim from the farmer. The second verse incorporates a quote from Walter van Tilburg Clark, author of "The Ox-Bow Incident," which says, "night is like a room. It makes the little things inside your head too important." "An East Wind is the laziest wind. It doesn't go around you. It goes through you."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: A song from "The Grand Bounce," this track opens with a poignant meteorological observation: "An East Wind is the laziest wind. It doesn't go around you. It goes through you." This line, almost verbatim, was shared with Downie by a farmer and incorporated into the song, which also contains quotes from Al Purdy and Walter von Tilburg Clark. "An East Wind is the laziest wind. It doesn't go around you. It goes through you. And that's absolutely true if you live in the Great Lakes, isn't it?"
